B6a-12-root-tip-longitudinal-section

Longitudinal section of a root tip (e.g. bean radicle) arranged vertically with the tip at the bottom. Show the root cap of loose cells at the very tip; just above it a zone of small, closely packed, dividing cells with large nuclei (some cells shown in mitosis); above that a zone of long, vacuolated, elongating cells; and at the top a zone of differentiated cells with root hairs growing out of the epidermis and visible xylem and phloem strands in the centre. Use brackets on the right side marking each zone.
B6a-01-plant-animal-support-comparison

Two side-by-side panels comparing support and movement. Left panel: a tall plant (e.g. a pawpaw or young mango tree) with leaves held up towards the sun, flowers held high with a bee visiting, a shoot tip bending towards the sun, and roots spreading in the soil. Right panel: an outline of a goat with its skeleton faintly visible, walking towards a patch of grass. Small arrows show the direction of movement in each. Soft greens and browns.
B6a-02-plant-supporting-tissues

A panel of five enlarged plant supporting tissues drawn side by side, each in transverse section with a small longitudinal section below. (1) Parenchyma: rounded thin-walled living cells with large vacuoles and air spaces. (2) Collenchyma: polygonal living cells with walls thickened at the corners. (3) Sclerenchyma fibres: very thick, evenly lignified walls with a small empty lumen, and in long section long cells with tapering overlapping ends; include one rounded sclereid (stone cell) with layered thick walls. (4) Xylem: a wide vessel with lignified walls, plus long sections showing annular, spiral and pitted thickening. (5) Phloem fibres beside sieve tubes and companion cells. Lignified walls in reddish-brown, cellulose walls in pale green.
B6a-03-dicot-root-transverse-section

Transverse section of a young dicotyledonous root (e.g. bean), drawn as a plan diagram. Show the piliferous layer with root hairs, a wide parenchyma cortex, the endodermis, the pericycle, and a central star-shaped xylem with four arms, with phloem groups between the arms. Shade the xylem dark reddish-brown to show it is the main supporting tissue in the centre, and add a small arrow diagram beside it showing a downward pulling force.
B6a-04-dicot-monocot-stem-sections

Two transverse sections of young stems drawn as plan diagrams, side by side. Left: dicotyledonous stem (sunflower), circular, with epidermis, a ring of collenchyma just under the epidermis, a parenchyma cortex, a ring of about eight vascular bundles each with a cap of sclerenchyma fibres on the outside, phloem, cambium and xylem, and a large central pith. Right: monocotyledonous stem (maize), circular, with epidermis, a hypodermal band of sclerenchyma, and many small vascular bundles scattered through the ground tissue, each surrounded by a sclerenchyma sheath, more crowded towards the edge. Shade all supporting tissues (collenchyma in light green, sclerenchyma and xylem in reddish-brown).
B6a-05-leaf-midrib-transverse-section

Transverse section through the midrib region of a dicotyledonous leaf, drawn as a detailed diagram. Show the upper epidermis with cuticle, palisade mesophyll, spongy mesophyll with air spaces, lower epidermis with a stoma, and the thickened midrib with collenchyma under both upper and lower epidermis, a large vascular bundle with xylem on the upper side and phloem on the lower side, and an arc of sclerenchyma fibres around the bundle. Add a small inset showing a whole leaf with its network of veins acting as a framework.
B6a-06-phototropism-seedling-experiment-setup

Experimental set-up for phototropism. Left: a cardboard box cut away to show a pot of young bean or maize seedlings inside; a narrow slit on the right side of the box lets in a beam of light (yellow rays), and the seedlings' shoots are bent towards the slit. Right (control): an identical pot of seedlings in open, all-round light, growing straight up.
B6a-07-geotropism-clinostat-experiment

Geotropism experiment with a clinostat. Left: a stationary cork disc with three bean seedlings pinned horizontally, their radicles curved downwards and their plumules curved upwards,. Right: an identical cork disc mounted on the horizontal axle of a small motorised clinostat with a curved arrow showing slow rotation; its seedlings remain straight and horizontal. Moist cotton wool around the seeds.
B6a-08-hydrotropism-experiment-apparatus

Hydrotropism experiment. A wire-mesh sieve hung at an angle, filled with brown moist sawdust containing germinating bean seeds. Roots have grown downwards through the mesh into the dry air and then curved back upwards to grow along the underside of the mesh towards the moist sawdust. Small blue droplets in the sawdust show moisture.
B6a-09-climbing-plants-tendril

Two climbing plants side by side. Left: a cucumber or passion fruit stem with a tendril that has touched a thin wooden stake and coiled tightly around it, and the part between the stake and the stem twisted like a spring; an enlarged inset of the tendril shows longer cells on the outer side and shorter cells on the side touching the stake. Right: a yam vine twining around a tall wooden stake in a farm mound.
B6a-10-tactic-movements-biology

Two panels showing tactic movements. Left: a Petri dish half covered by black card with a lamp shining on the uncovered half; many tiny green Chlamydomonas cells crowded in the lit half and few in the dark half; an enlarged inset of a single Chlamydomonas with two flagella, a red eyespot, a cup-shaped chloroplast and a nucleus, with an arrow pointing towards the light. Right: an enlarged moss or fern archegonium (flask-shaped with a neck and an egg at the base) with several small flagellated sperm swimming in a water film towards the open neck, and dotted lines showing a chemical spreading out from the neck.
B6a-14-shoot-tip-longitudinal-section

Longitudinal section of a shoot tip (terminal bud). Show a dome-shaped apical meristem at the top, young leaf primordia as small bumps on either side, older young leaves curving over the dome to protect it, small axillary bud primordia in the axils of the leaves, developing procambium strands, and below this a zone of elongating cells and then a zone of differentiated tissues. Mark nodes and internodes on the stem below.
B6a-15-auxin-phototropism-mechanism

Three-step diagram of auxin and phototropism in a shoot or oat coleoptile. Step 1: a straight shoot with light from the right; dots representing auxin at the tip, evenly spread. Step 2: auxin dots moving to the left (shaded) side and down that side; cells on the shaded side drawn longer than cells on the lit side. Step 3: the shoot bent towards the light on the right. Arrows show the direction of light and auxin movement.
B6a-16-auxin-geotropism-response

Diagram of a bean seedling placed horizontally showing auxin and geotropism. Top: the seedling lying on its side with dots (auxin) collecting on the lower side of both the plumule (shoot) and the radicle (root), with a downward arrow labelled gravity. Bottom: the same seedling a day later, with the shoot curving upwards (lower side cells longer) and the root curving downwards (upper side cells longer). Small enlarged cell diagrams show long cells on the lower side of the shoot and long cells on the upper side of the root.
